text: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his steadfast love endures forever.
Let Israel say it: his steadfast love endures forever.
Let the house of Aaron say it: his steadfast love endures forever.
Let those who fear the LORD say it: his steadfast love endures forever.
Out of my distress I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me and set me in a wide-open place.

versions.text: Out of my distress I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me and set me free.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew imagery contrasts the 'narrow place' (מֵצַר, distress) with a 'broad, spacious place' (מֶרְחָב). 'Set me free' loses this deliberate narrow/wide wordplay, which is one of the strongest oral features of the verse.

text: The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?
The LORD is on my side, he is my helper; I will look in triumph on those who hate me.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in any human being.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in princes.
All the nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
They surrounded me, yes, they closed in on me; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
They swarmed around me like bees, but they were snuffed out like a fire of thorns; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
You pushed me hard, so that I was falling, but the LORD helped me.

versions.text: I was pushed hard, about to fall, but the LORD helped me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb דְחִיתַנִי is second person singular ('you pushed me'), a direct address to the enemy. The passive rendering removes the direct address and obscures who is acting. The second-person form also keeps the vivid, dramatic tone that reads well aloud.

text: The LORD is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation.
Shouts of joy and victory ring out in the tents of the righteous: "The right hand of the LORD does mighty things!
The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does mighty things!"
I shall not die, but live, and tell of what the LORD has done.
The LORD has disciplined me severely, but he has not handed me over to death.
Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and give thanks to the LORD.
This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.
I thank you, for you answered me; you have become my salvation.
The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
O LORD, save us, we pray! O LORD, grant us success, we pray!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD. From the house of the LORD we bless you.
The LORD is God, and he has given us light. Bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give you thanks; you are my God, and I will exalt you.
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his steadfast love endures forever.
